question: Evaluate: (−9) − (−60) ÷ (−6) + (−4) × 6
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply BODMAS rule directly to solve the expression:

First calculate division: (−60) ÷ (−6) = 10

Then calculate multiplication: (−4) × 6 = −24

Add the results to the remaining terms:

⇒ −9 − 10 + (−24) = −43

**∴ The correct answer is −43.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(−9) − (−60) ÷ (−6) + (−4) × 6

**Formula Used:**

BODMAS Rule (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

**Calculations:**

⇒ (−9) − [(−60) ÷ (−6)] + [(−4) × 6]

⇒ (−9) − (10) + (−24)

⇒ −9 − 10 − 24

⇒ −19 − 24

⇒ −43

**∴ The correct answer is −43.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It defines the order of operations: Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction. Always perform division and multiplication before addition and subtraction.

Sign Rules for Multiplication & Division

When operating on numbers with the same sign, the result is positive (− ÷ − = +). When signs are different, the result is negative (+ × − = −).

Sign Rules for Addition & Subtraction

When adding multiple negative numbers, add their absolute values and keep the negative sign (e.g., −a − b − c = −(a + b + c)).
